messages:
maya: 🚨 Just got paged by oncall-bot for high pagerstream volume on embeddings cluster (eu-west). Root says >5m sustained error-rate spike. Anyone oncall?

jordan: oncall here. seeing a bunch of 503s from model-worker instances. Not a full outage but noise is spiking.

oncall-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-4391. Paging group: #eng-oncall. Initial severity: P2.

maya: thanks. quick context — traffic to emb-service spiked after a customer bulk re-ingestion job at ~09:12 UTC. Could be KV cache thrash + autoscale delay.

devon: confirming autoscaler did open some nodes but worker churn is high, and there are evictions in the logs: 
```
evict: container cpu 98% -> oom_kill pid=4021
2026-03-15T09:16:42Z model-worker[4021]: kv cache miss rate 0.87
```

lena: FYI customer affected: acme-analytics; they reported timeouts from their ingestion pipeline. Support ticket linked in INC-2026-4391.

jordan: mitigation plan: 1) pause bulk re-ingestion if customer still running 2) pin critical model variants to cached nodes 3) increase alert squelch for transient 502/503 burst to avoid pager storms. Thoughts?

maya: +1. for pinning — can we route acme traffic to a dedicated pool temporarily?

devon: we have a spare small pool in eu-west-d. I'll do a temporary route using the runtime gating config: 
```
POST /internal/routing/override
{
  "customer": "acme-analytics",
  "pool": "dedicated-spare-eu-west-d",
  "ttl": 1800
}
```

infra-bot: Routing override applied by devon at 09:23 UTC.

jordan: paused the re-ingestion job with the customer — support confirmed. Monitoring traffic drop now.

maya: good. on alerts: current pager triggers on 1m error_rate > 3% across cluster. That threshold is too sensitive for short bursts. Proposal: change pager rule to 5m window and 2% sustained, and add a burst-only metric that logs but doesn't page.

lena: agree on reducing noise. But we need to annotate runbook so oncall knows the reasoning and rollback steps. I'll open a small PR to the oncall playbook.

devon: patch for routing and squelch implemented. Creating dashboard tile for "pagerstream corridor" (shows 1m/5m error_rate, evictions, kv-cache miss rate). Link: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/pgsnoisecorridor/overview

maya: can someone own the runbook update and link to the dashboard + the PR? We should also set an owner for the threshold change and a rollback button.

jordan: I'll own the runbook edit. Will add: 
- rationale (reduce pages during customer bursts)
- exact alert rule change (1m -> 5m, page when >2% sustained)
- temporary squelch policy (10m after routing override)
- rollback steps (revert routing override, restore original alert rule)

lena: tagging infra + SRE for review @devon @maya. Also adding a cross-ref to INC-2026-4391 in the playbook.

devon: small note — add a line about KV cache warmup: if miss_rate stays >0.6 for >10m, escalate to infra (possible cache flush needed).

jordan: added that note. PR: https://git.redwood.internal/oncall/playbooks/pulls/58 — please review.

maya: reviewed and left comments. Two minor edits: clarify timeline expectations for customers, and add a once-off alert that notifies support instead of paging when it's only 1 customer affected.

lena: good call. I'll add the support-only notification block.

infra-bot: Alert rule updated (draft) by jordan at 09:36 UTC: rule_id=reroute-error-agg. Old: window=1m threshold=3% (page). New draft: window=5m threshold=2% (page), 1m threshold=3% (log only).

jordan: rolling the change to staging first.

maya: customer impact note for post-incident summary: acme-analytics experienced 1.8x latency and ~12% of their ingestion requests retried between 09:12–09:28 UTC. No data loss reported. Support SLA incident opened.

lena: after-action items: 
- jordan: merge playbook PR and annotate runbook with dashboard links (owner)
- devon: add cache-warmup monitor and eviction counter to the corridor dashboard
- maya: coordinate with support to confirm acme back to normal and close the support ticket
- infra: consider autoscaler tuning to avoid churn during sudden customer re-ingestion spikes

jordan: PR merged at 09:48 UTC. Runbook link: https://git.redwood.internal/oncall/playbooks/blob/main/pagerstream-noise.md

devon: added eviction counter and kv cache tile. Dashboard link updated in runbook.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-4391 resolved at 09:52 UTC. Summary: transient customer-induced load + cache thrash caused elevated error rates. Mitigations: routing override, customer pause, alert squelch change. Postmortem scheduled.

maya: closing loop — supports confirms acme ingestion resumed at normal rate and retries cleared. Good job team. :tada:

lena: filing postmortem and linking to PR/dashboards/ticket. I'll assign owners for follow-up items.

jordan: leaving a follow-up note in the handoff doc for next oncall: if you see repeated noise from a single customer, consider routing + squelch first before mass scaling.

maya: thanks all. I'll add a short blurb in the customer-facing incident summary.

lena: done — adding metadata and owners in the postmortem doc.

jordan: good to head out. handoff to next oncall in 20m.

devon: leaving logs and grep snippets in the incident ticket for future debugging.

maya: +1, great coordination.
